title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the handwritten verso of a page of Deligne's 'Courbes elliptiques : formulaire d'après J. Tate' (LNM 476, 1975). The note faces §6 on the normal forms and automorphisms of curves with j = 0 and j = 1728. Grothendieck poses a 'question connexe' about how the j-invariant behaves locally on the deformation space.

Setup: E is an elliptic curve over a perfect field k, and M^ is the formal moduli (universal deformation) space of E over W(k). This is Spf W(k)[[t]], with t a relative regular parameter. Aut(E) acts on M^.

Boxed claim: the completion of the j-line at j(E) is the quotient of the deformation space by Aut(E), i.e. Spec W(k)[[j - j(E)]]^ ≅ M^/Aut(E). Equivalently, W(k)[[t]]^{Aut(E)} = W(k)[[j - j0]], since the coarse moduli space of elliptic curves is the j-line. The task is then a local study of j as a function of t.

The cases:
(a) j = 0, p ≠ 2, 3: Aut = μ6, so Aut/{±1} = μ3 acts tamely and j ~ t^3.
(b) j = 1728 = 12^3, p ≠ 2, 3: Aut = μ4, Aut/{±1} = μ2, so j ~ t^2.
(c) j = 0, p = 3: Aut/{±1} has 6 elements, and the action is wild.
(d) j = 0, p = 2: Aut/{±1} has 12 elements.

Marginal consequence for equal characteristic: in characteristic 3, 6 | v(j); in characteristic 2, 12 | v(j). These are the valuations of j for a curve over an equal-characteristic DVR with good reduction at the supersingular point j = 0. They follow from the Weierstrass forms:
- Char 3: y^2 = x^3 + a2 x^2 + a4 x + a6 gives c4 = a2^2 and j = a2^6/Δ, with supersingular locus a2 = 0. So j = unit · t^6.
- Char 2: the deformation y^2 + a1 xy + a3 y = x^3 + ... gives c4 = a1^4 and j = a1^12/Δ. So j = unit · t^12.

Bottom line: a tentative identification of the order-24 group in Deligne's (V), which carries a '?' on the facing typescript page. Grothendieck proposes the semidirect product Q8 ⋊ Z/3, with Z/3 permuting (i, j, k) cyclically. This is SL2(F3), the correct answer.
errors: No mathematical errors found. Statements (a) through (d) and the divisibilities 6 | v(j) (char 3) and 12 | v(j) (char 2) are consistent with the standard Weierstrass computations.
Possible imprecision: in (c) and (d) the 'group of 6 / 12 elements' should be read as Aut(E)/{±1}, which is the group acting effectively on the deformation space. Aut(E) itself has orders 12 and 24.

The boxed quotient statement in mixed characteristic with wild action (p = 2, 3) is true because the coarse moduli space is A^1_j. However, the quotient is not computed by the tame-quotient argument; the note leaves this as 'étude locale à faire'.

ideas.what: The complete local ring of the j-line at j(E) equals the Aut(E)-invariants of the universal deformation ring W(k)[[t]].
ideas.modern_name: Coarse moduli space as quotient of the universal deformation space by the automorphism group (étale/formal local structure of the coarse moduli of M_{1,1})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Rapoport (1973); Katz–Mazur (1985); standard in stacks theory
ideas.where_published: The general principle (formal moduli, quotients by finite groups) appears in SGA 1 and FGA; this specific j-line statement is not known to be in Grothendieck's published texts.

ideas.what: Local behaviour of j in the deformation parameter: j ~ t^3 at j = 0 and j ~ t^2 at j = 1728 for p ≠ 2, 3; ramification of order 6 and 12 at the supersingular point j = 0 for p = 3 and p = 2.
ideas.modern_name: Ramification of the j-map M_{1,1} → A^1 at curves with extra automorphisms; the j-invariant as a function on the Lubin–Tate/Serre–Tate deformation space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Deligne's formulaire after Tate; Silverman's AEC Appendix A; Katz–Mazur)

ideas.what: In equal characteristic 3 (resp. 2), a curve with good supersingular reduction has 6 | v(j) (resp. 12 | v(j)).
ideas.modern_name: Valuation of j at supersingular reduction in characteristic 2 and 3 (wild potentially good reduction)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; follows from Tate's formulaire; related to work on wild potentially good reduction (e.g. Kraus 1990)

ideas.what: Aut of the supersingular curve in characteristic 2 is Q8 ⋊ Z/3 with Z/3 permuting i, j, k.
ideas.modern_name: Aut(E) ≅ SL2(F3), the binary tetrahedral group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Deuring); Silverman AEC Appendix A, Exercise A.1

deep.surprise_reason: These are marginal reading notes on Deligne's formulaire. Grothendieck checks and reorganises the j = 0 / j = 1728 cases through the deformation-space quotient, and correctly identifies the order-24 group as SL2(F3). All of this is standard and well documented in the literature (Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur, Silverman). There is nothing new beyond confirming that he read and commented on the formulaire.
transcription_corrections: 'Spec W(k)[j]^' should probably read 'Spec W(k)[[j]]^' (completed local ring of the j-line), or Spf.
'|| = car 3' / '= car 2' is likely shorthand for 'égale caractéristique 3 / 2' (equal-characteristic case). The marks are not a literal parallel sign.
In (c) and (d), 'groupe 6 éléments' and '12' refer to Aut(E)/{±1} acting on the formal moduli.
Bottom line: 'semi direct de Z/3 par {±1 ±i ±j ±k} où Z/3 agit par (i,j,k)', i.e. Q8 ⋊ Z/3 with cyclic permutation of i, j, k.
